concerns.text: T024e selects 'ALL available datasets' or the first 50 alphabetically. This silently relaxes FR-004 (6-hour time limit) and SC-004 (runtime feasibility). The task lacks a mechanism to enforce the 6-hour cap or dynamically reduce the subset size based on estimated runtime, risking a violation of the hard time constraint defined in the spec.

T031 calculates 'Recovery Ratio' using T015a (Seed 42) as the denominator. While T015a satisfies FR-001's re-computation requirement, the task description does not explicitly enforce the exclusion of datasets where the 'GPU-Tuned' baseline metric type (AUC vs RMSE) mismatches the 'CPU-Conditioned' metric type. The spec's Assumptions section mandates this exclusion to prevent invalid ratio calculations, but the task logic omits this validation step.

T034 applies FDR correction ONLY to correlation p-values (T033) and explicitly excludes t-test results (T035). SC-003 states 'with FDR correction applied for multiple features' in the context of the t-test success criterion. The task's explicit exclusion of the t-test from FDR correction creates a semantic conflict with the success criterion's phrasing, potentially weakening the statistical rigor required by SC-003 if the t-test is considered part of the 'family' of tests in the spec's intent.

T060 triggers a 'Small Sample Warning' if N < 30. The spec's US-003 Independent Test (Acceptance Scenario 1) explicitly requires flagging a shortfall only if 'fewer than 20 datasets are available'. T060's threshold of 30 is a silent relaxation of the spec's explicit acceptance criterion, potentially causing the system to fail a spec-defined test case (N=25) by flagging it as a warning when the spec only requires a flag for N<20, or conversely, failing to flag a critical issue if the spec intended N<30 but wrote N<20. This is a scope mismatch.

T045/T045b mandate skipping zero-variance features and excluding datasets where ALL features are zero-variance. FR-003 requires computing metadata statistics for 'all structured tabular features'. If a dataset is excluded entirely due to zero variance, the task fails to satisfy the 'all datasets' implication of FR-003 without a documented fallback or justification in the spec. The task logic is aggressive and risks violating the requirement to analyze the full dataset subset defined in the spec's assumptions.
